The 90% prediction interval for this value, when applied to a laboratory not included in the training data, ranges from 0.182 mg/g to 105 mg/g. This wide interval reflects the uncertainty in the prediction, particularly due to the equilibrium concentration (Ce) of 347 mg/L, which is outside the laboratory range of 0.00303-195 mg/L, indicating that this value is an extrapolation along the fitted isotherm.

The contributions to this prediction include an equilibrium concentration multiplier of 11.01, a polymer type multiplier of 1.63, an ageing status multiplier of 0.71, and an adsorption system multiplier of 0.82. These factors influence the adsorption behavior as seen in the literature, where pH and surface charge characteristics also play significant roles in Cu(II) adsorption on microplastics [Source: Xiao_2026; Muthuraja_2024].

The field-scale value, calculated using the laboratory qe and a field-to-laboratory ratio of 0.22, results in a field-scale value of 0.983 mg/g. This ratio indicates that the adsorption capacity in field conditions is significantly lower than in laboratory settings, with a confidence interval ranging from 0.12 to 8.1 mg/g.

WARNING: The equilibrium concentration (Ce) of 347 mg/L is outside the laboratory range, meaning the prediction is based on extrapolation. Additionally, one local measurement would narrow the prediction interval significantly, changing it to a range multiplied and divided by 2.5.

facts:
Inputs: polymer PP; Virgin particles; Mixed system; Ce = 347 mg/L.
Predicted laboratory-equilibrium qe: 4.384 mg/g.
90% prediction interval for a laboratory not in the training data: 0.182 to 105 mg/g (prediction multiplied and divided by 24.1).
With one local measurement for the same material the interval narrows to the prediction multiplied and divided by 2.5.
Field-to-laboratory ratio (dimensionless): 0.22, 95% confidence interval 0.027 to 1.8, from 4 field studies.
Field-scale value (laboratory qe times that ratio): 0.983 mg/g; with the confidence interval of the ratio it ranges from 0.12 to 8.1 mg/g.
Effect of each input on the prediction, as a multiplier of qe relative to the average laboratory observation: equilibrium concentration multiplies qe by 11.01; polymer type multiplies qe by 1.63; ageing status multiplies qe by 0.71; adsorption system multiplies qe by 0.82.
Model: pooled Freundlich isotherm fitted to 871 observations from 29 studies; Freundlich exponent 0.51; laboratory Ce range 0.00303-195 mg/L; PP is represented by 8 studies.
WARNING: Ce = 347 mg/L is outside the laboratory range (0.00303-195 mg/L); the value is an extrapolation along the fitted isotherm.
